tasks.title: Build ollama.New with host resolution, host parsing and refusals
steps: Write TS-28-1 to TS-28-8 as external tests (package ollama_test) and confirm they fail

In provider/ollama add `Options{Host string; Env map[string]string; Getenv func(string) string; HTTPClient *http.Client; Now func() time.Time; Warnf func(string, ...any)}` and `type Client` with Host() string

Implement the OLLAMA_HOST lookup as in provider/anthropic client.go providerEnv.Lookup: Options.Host first (no variable read at all), then Env (empty falls through), then Getenv when non-nil, else os.LookupEnv; only the key HostVar is ever asked

Implement host parsing by Ollama CLI rules: trim; no scheme means http and port 11434; http:// without port means 80; https:// without port 443; keep path; reject other schemes, unparseable values and ports outside 1-65535 with an error wrapping ErrInvalidHost

Refuse user information (message shows the host with password redacted, e.g. via url.Redacted-style logic, never containing the password) and ollama.com or any *.ollama.com host (message says the hosted service is not supported), both wrapping ErrInvalidHost; accept notollama.com

New(m, opts) (*Client, error): fail with an "ollama:"-prefixed error when strings.TrimSpace(m.ID) is empty; make no network request; store the model, resolved *url.URL, Now (default time.Now) and Warnf (nil discards)
Confirm `var _ core.ProviderClient = (*Client)(nil)` once Stream exists; for now add the Stream method with `panic("not implemented")` only if needed to compile, to be replaced by the next task
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`

tasks.title: Stream core: credential-free transport, base request, text and thinking decode, final message
steps: Write TS-28-9, 10, 11, 26, 27 and 30 using an httptest recording server that serves application/x-ndjson lines, and confirm they fail; put recorder helpers in provider/ollama/recorder_test.go

Add an http.RoundTripper wrapper that deletes the Authorization header on a clone of the request then delegates to Options.HTTPClient's Transport (http.DefaultTransport when nil); build the SDK client with api.NewClient(base, &http.Client{Transport: wrapper}) in New, never api.ClientFromEnvironment
Implement (*Client).Stream: return (nil, ctx.Err()) for a done context; otherwise core.StreamChannel over a core.NewEventStream driven by a goroutine, mirroring provider/anthropic/stream.go

Build api.ChatRequest: Model = m.ID, Stream = &true, Truncate = &false, Options["num_ctx"] = m.ContextWindow or catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow when not positive; send via client.Chat with a callback per ChatResponse

Create a decode state mirroring anthropic's decodeState: emitStart pushes MessageStartEvent{Model: m.ID, Effort: req.Effort, Timestamp: Now()}; thinking chunks stream as ThinkingStart/Delta and content as TextStart/Delta, closing the open block on a kind switch, appending each completed block and pushing MessageUpdateEvent; thinking never becomes text

On the done chunk after its own content: push TextEnd/ThinkingEnd/ToolCallEnd in block order, build the final message (StopReasonLength for done_reason length, else StopReasonToolUse if tool calls, else StopReasonStop; RawStopReason verbatim; ResponseModel from chunk), push MessageEndEvent and end the stream with the message and nil Err
Leave tool-call decode, usage, and error classification to later tasks but give a stub-free minimal path (a non-done end currently ends with ErrStreamTruncated)
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`

tasks.title: Decode tool calls with wire key order and unique ids, report netted zero-cost usage, prove concurrency safety
steps: Write TS-28-28, 29, 31, 40 and 41 (property tests with testing/quick or a generator loop; TS-28-31 with 32 goroutines under -race) and confirm they fail

For each message.tool_calls entry build the ToolUseBlock via core.NewToolUse(id, name, json.Marshal(call.Function.Arguments)); confirm via `go doc` that ToolCallFunctionArguments marshals in insertion order and that the SDK's ToolCall has an ID; absent arguments become {}
Push ToolCallStartEvent then exactly one ToolInputDeltaEvent carrying the whole argument JSON, then append the block; ToolCallEndEvent comes at the done chunk in block order
When a call has no id, synthesize one from a per-Client atomic counter (e.g. `ollama_call_<n>`) so ids are unique within and across responses

From the done chunk compute Usage: InputTokens = max(0, PromptEvalCount - PromptEvalCachedCount), CacheReadTokens only when cached > 0, OutputTokens = EvalCount, Requests = 1, SetCost(0) so the presence bit is set; no reasoning tokens; use core.Usage.SetField/SetCost
Ensure the Client holds no per-stream mutable state outside the decode state and atomic counter so concurrent Stream calls race-free
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`

tasks.title: Replay the transcript: message order, repair, thinking, tool calls and results
steps: Write TS-28-12, 19, 20, 21 (property test over generated JSON objects with non-alphabetical, nested and unicode keys, comparing key order in the raw recorded body) and 22, and confirm they fail
Build messages in order: one system message with the text blocks of Request.System joined by "\n\n" (omitted when empty), then Request.Prefix, then the repaired Request.Messages
Pass Request.Messages through provider.RepairToolPairing before encoding; never mutate the input slice; when the repair changed anything call Options.Warnf once with the report (nil Warnf discards)

Encode core.UserMessage as role user with its text; core.AssistantMessage as role assistant with text content, thinking = concatenated non-redacted thinking text only when the message's Model == m.ID (other thinking is dropped, never content), and one api.ToolCall per ToolUseBlock with ID, Function.Index = position among the message's calls, Name and Arguments
Decode ToolUseBlock.Input into the SDK's ToolCallFunctionArguments with json.Unmarshal so key order is kept (verify with `go doc`); the recorded raw body must show Input's key order
Encode each core.ToolResultMessage as one role tool message with Content = provider.ToolResultText(result) (Error: prefix for errors), ToolName and ToolCallID, in transcript order
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`

tasks.title: Encode num_predict, sampling, tools, tool choice and effort as think
steps: Write TS-28-13 to TS-28-18 and TS-28-23 to TS-28-25 and confirm they fail; TS-28-25 uses catalog.Select("ollama","STANDARD","")
Set options.num_predict: requested MaxTokens when positive and not above m.MaxOutputTokens, else m.MaxOutputTokens when positive, else requested when positive, else omit
Set options.temperature (including an explicit 0), top_p and stop only when set on the request; never set keep_alive, format or images

Declare each core.ToolWire as a function api.Tool in request order: json.Marshal the InputSchema and json.Unmarshal into api.ToolFunctionParameters (so additionalProperties, format and bounds drop); a nil schema becomes {"type":"object","properties":{}}; a decode failure ends the turn before any request with an "ollama:" error naming the tool (use core.ErrorStream-style failure, no HTTP attempt)
ToolChoiceNone sends no tools key at all; unset and auto send the tools

Implement applyThink like provider/anthropic applyThinking: empty effort or ThinkingKindNone sends none; nil Efforts map sends string(effort); with a map, absent or nil sends none, else strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(*v)) as api.ThinkValue{Value: string}; never clamp
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`

tasks.title: Classify failures: truncation, cancellation, unreachable, 404, context window, auth and other statuses
steps: Write TS-28-32 to TS-28-39 and TS-28-42 against the recording server (closed port for unreachable, a blocking handler for cancellation) and confirm they fail

Implement fail(text, err) like anthropic's decodeState.fail: an abort gives StopReasonAborted, ErrorMessage "Request was aborted", Err core.ErrAborted and no ErrorEvent; any other failure gives StopReasonError, a terminal ErrorEvent, then MessageEndEvent; use the caller's context (not the derived one) to detect cancellation, which takes precedence over every other classification; cancel must stop the request within 1 second
A Chat return or stream end without a done chunk ends with an error wrapping ErrStreamTruncated; the failed message keeps streamed text and thinking and drops every tool call (also on abort)

Classify errors from client.Chat: net.OpError/dial failure wraps ErrUnreachable (names host, `ollama serve`, OLLAMA_HOST); api.StatusError 404 wraps ErrModelNotFound and also yields *ollama.StatusError{Code:404} via errors.As (names model, host, Ollama's message, `ollama pull <model>`)

Recognise a message saying the input exceeds the context length (status error or in-stream error) as ErrContextWindow: text names the model and the num_ctx sent, includes Ollama's message and says a model already loaded at a smaller length keeps it until it unloads

401/403 give a *StatusError text naming the host, saying AgentKit sends no credential to Ollama and to check OLLAMA_HOST; other statuses give *StatusError{Code, Text: "ollama: HTTP <code>: <message>"}; an in-stream error line becomes an "ollama:"-prefixed error with Ollama's message classified by the same rules
Make exactly one HTTP attempt per Stream call (no retries); every error text starts with "ollama:" and never includes any environment variable value other than the host
A failed turn's Usage has Requests 1 and no input, output or cache-read presence bits
Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`
